finding.claim: The ban endpoint catches the 403 raised by require_admin and carries on, so any user who can reach the route can ban any account. abort(403) raises werkzeug HTTPException, which subclasses Exception. The broad `except Exception` swallows it and only logs a warning. do_ban(uid) then runs and the handler returns ok=True. The sibling unban route calls require_admin without the try/except, which confirms the intended behavior.
finding.source: Any authenticated non-admin user (g.user without is_admin) sending POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban with an arbitrary uid
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20, the privileged ban operation

trace.note: Route /admin/users/<uid>/ban accepts POST with attacker-controlled uid
require_admin(g.user) is called, and for a non-admin it reaches abort(403) at line 11
Only a warning is logged and execution continues instead of re-raising or returning

finding.guards_checked: require_admin is the only guard and it is neutralized by the try/except. No before_request hook, decorator or other middleware in the repo enforces admin access. g.user is never set in this file, so that is assumed to happen elsewhere. The unban route is correctly guarded, so the flaw is specific to ban. Reproduction: POST /admin/users/<victim>/ban as a non-admin returns 200 {ok:true} and the ban executes. The log line also writes the user name, which is minor.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) aborts with 403 for non-admins, but the call at admin.py:17 sits inside try/except Exception (16-19) that swallows the HTTPException. No before_request hook or decorator exists in the repo.
verdict.reason: admin.py:17-20 calls require_admin inside `except Exception`, which swallows the abort(403) from admin.py:11 and only logs, so do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 runs for any authenticated non-admin, unlike the unguarded-by-try unban at admin.py:26.
